subject.title: Google Chat: markdown renders as raw text; typing indicator says 'OpenClaw is typing' instead of app name

question: Should Google Chat outbound text be converted to Google Chat's supported formatting syntax, stripped to plain text, or split so only the typing identity fallback lands now?
rationale: Source evidence proves both current OpenClaw paths still send the reported output, but the closed Markdown PR and current Google docs leave the rendering policy as a product choice rather than a mechanical fix.

options.title: Render Google Chat Syntax
options.body: Add a Google Chat-specific Markdown renderer/chunker plus the typing identity fallback in the plugin, with focused tests for replies and message-tool sends.

options.title: Strip To Plain Text
options.body: Normalize Google Chat outbound text to plain text everywhere, accepting loss of supported bold/italic/link formatting for a simpler UX.

options.title: Land Typing Only
options.body: Accept the identity fallback as a narrow fix now and keep Markdown rendering as a separately scoped policy/design issue.

recommendation.title: Render Google Chat Syntax
recommendation.body: Add a Google Chat-specific Markdown renderer/chunker plus the typing identity fallback in the plugin, with focused tests for replies and message-tool sends.

likelyOwner.reason: The decision spans Google Chat channel behavior and shared outbound formatting, areas where this history shows broad recent ownership.
